articleTitle: Knowledge-guided Aspect-based Summarization
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Communications, Computing and Artificial Intelligence (CCCAI)
abstract: Contextualized pre-trained models, such as BERT [1] and BART [2], have shown great potential in various NLP tasks, pushing the state-of-the-art results to a new level. Although studies have shown that those pre-trained models have captured different kinds of knowledge due to the massive corpus they have been trained on [3], injecting task-specific external knowledge often shows further improvement [4]. Here we choose aspect-based abstractive summarization as a case study and explore two different ways to inject external knowledge into BART. One is through a knowledge graph, the other is through human-defined sequence-level scores. Experiment results show that both methods can get an improvement over vanilla BART.

articleTitle: Synthesizing Virtual Night Scene on OpenStreetMap
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Communications, Computing and Artificial Intelligence (CCCAI)
abstract: As modern game development technologies are emerging rapidly, virtual content synthesis for immersive gaming experiences became a popular research topic recently. Especially, as the game genres driven by modern life experiences within realistic virtual urban environments are gaining popularity, efficient and effective modeling approaches for synthesizing realistic urban environments are necessary. As a procedural modeling approach, synthesizing realistic urban scenes using OpenStreetMap (OSM) can result in satisfying results without demanding heavy manual efforts from game content designers. However, existing works that synthesize realistic virtual urban environments using OSM have not proposed the technical approach and experiment results that present realistic night scenes of virtual urban environments. Therefore, in this paper, we propose a novel procedural modeling approach to automatically synthesize realistic virtual night scenes on OpenStreetMap. The experiment results of synthesized urban night scenes validate the efficacy of our proposed technical approach.

articleTitle: Study on Radiation Impact of 4G Mobile Communication System on Human Body by EEG in Dhaka
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Communications, Computing and Artificial Intelligence (CCCAI)
abstract: The intention of our research is to determine the radiation impact of 4G mobile communication on the human body. While mobile phones are being used, they emit very little nonionizing radiation. Through this work, we measured the Specific Absorption Rate (SAR) using the developed circuit to assess mobile phone radiation. The information was gathered at two different locations in Dhaka, Bangladesh, at different times and dates. From this study, it was observed that a cellular phone’s SAR is significantly greater during the conversation. Moreover, when there is no phone conversation, the radiation of the phone is lowered. When the mobile phone is close to the base station, the SAR is around 0.2724Wkg<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>. EEG measurement was done to detect the impact of 4G mobile radiation on human body. Several alterations in the nervous system were investigated and low-voltage beta activity was detected while the test was conducted.

articleTitle: Research on Power Marketing Data Sharing Framework Based on Semi-supervised Vertical Federated Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Communications, Computing and Artificial Intelligence (CCCAI)
abstract: As the electric power industry deals with an expanding and diverse data landscape, secure and efficient data usage is crucial for intelligent systems. However, security constraints often lead to data isolation, hindering data sharing and access among departments, companies, and institutions. This results in data silos. To address these challenges, this paper introduces a novel data sharing framework that combines vertical federated learning and semi-supervised learning to overcome power marketing data sharing issues. Vertical federated learning facilitates cross-departmental data modeling while preserving data privacy and improving data analysis accuracy. Semi-supervised learning utilizes unaligned data from federated learning to enhance prediction accuracy and generalization. Empirical results demonstrate that this framework enhances data analysis accuracy and efficiency while maintaining data security and privacy. This approach presents new opportunities and challenges for cooperation and competition within the electric power industry.

articleTitle: Dynamic AP Association for UAV-Centric Aerial-Ground Communication with Cell-Free Massive MIMO
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Communications, Computing and Artificial Intelligence (CCCAI)
abstract: Cell-free massive multiple-input and multiple-output (MIMO) is a promising networking architecture for the sixth generation (6G) mobile communication networks, as it may effectively mitigate the severe inter-cell interference issue for cell boundary users. With cell-free massive MIMO, it is possible to provide communication services with uniform quality across the network. In this paper, we consider a cell-free massive MIMO unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) communication system, in which a number of access points (APs) simultaneously serve the UAV while eschewing traditional cell boundaries. A dynamic AP association strategy is proposed to achieve UAV-centric aerial-ground communications. In every time slot, the channels between UAV and APs are first estimated by uplink training. Each AP compares the estimated average power strength of the channel with a certain threshold, and only those APs whose average power strength is larger than the given threshold are activated to serve the UAV. Based on the proposed dynamic AP association strategy, we further derive the achievable communication rate with the estimated channel. Numerical results show that the proposed dynamic AP association scheme for cell-free massive MIMO system maintains good performance with flexible AP activations.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of NLP Models for Detecting Depression on Twitter
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Communications, Computing and Artificial Intelligence (CCCAI)
abstract: Depression is a serious mental health issue affecting a significant portion of the world’s population. With the widespread use of social media platforms, researchers have explored the possibility of utilizing natural language processing (NLP) techniques to detect signs of depression in users’ posts. In this paper, we present a comparative analysis of six different NLP models, namely BERT, RoBERTa, DistilBERT, ALBERT, Electra, and XLNet, for depression detection on Twitter data. The experiments compare the performance of different models, and the results reveal that the highest-performing models include XLNet, DistilBERT, and RoBERTa with the accuracies over 99%.

articleTitle: Anglo-Bangla Language-Based AI Chatbot for Bangladeshi University Admission System
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Communications, Computing and Artificial Intelligence (CCCAI)
abstract: Many Bangladeshi students face significant challenges during university admission because of a lack of communication. However, some of the usual chatbots have been implemented in English/Bangla. Most students are comfortable communicating in a slang mixture of Bengali and English (Anglo-Bangla). This article presents a language detection model for Anglo-Bangla using machine learning algorithms, including Logistic Regression (LR), Decision Tree (DT), K-Nearest Neighbours (KNN), Support Vector Machine (SVM), and Multinomial Naive Bias (MNB). The model is designed to assist the university admission process in Bangladesh through an automated chatbot system. The chatbot system utilizes the language detection model to understand and respond to the queries of potential students in English, Bengali, and Anglo-Bangla. When the chatbot is unable to provide a proper answer in rare cases, the system logs the query along with user contact information. University officials will then update the appropriate response and the system will send the response to the user via email or SMS. The detector continuously detects the language and creates separate datasets to improve the chatbot’s performance. Our model was trained on a dataset of 0.15 million conversations collected from Socian Ltd., a leading NLP company. The dataset consisted of unlabeled Bangla and Anglo-Bangla languages and an English dataset collected from Kaggle, which was a mixed-language dataset. The model’s performance shows that the Multinomial Naive Bayes algorithm yields the highest accuracy in detecting the following languages: 99.64% for the Mixed, 99.13% for English, 100% for Bangla, and 99.51% for Anglo-Bangla. The proposed model can be used to improve the performance of other multilingual chatbot systems and assist with tasks such as customer service, medical assistance, and data collection in polyglot societies.

articleTitle: A weakly supervised multi-instance learning based on graph neural network for breast cancer pathology image classification
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Communications, Computing and Artificial Intelligence (CCCAI)
abstract: Breast cancer is a malignant tumor that occurs in the breast, posing a serious threat to women’s health. Histopathological examination is an important means of breast cancer diagnosis, and the analysis of histopathological images is an important application of artificial intelligence in histopathological examination. Despite the remarkable achievements of convolutional neural networks (CNNs), there are still challenges in distinguishing between multiple subtypes and overcoming imbalanced datasets. Therefore, to overcome these challenges, this paper proposes a weakly supervised multi-instance learning model GMIL based on graph neural networks (GNNs) for breast cancer pathology image classification. The model consists of three modules: the feature extraction module for feature extraction, the GNN module for aggregating neighbor information, and the gated attention module for feature fusion. Multiple experiments on the BreakHis dataset show that the proposed model outperforms the latest algorithms in terms of performance.

articleTitle: Markov Model for French-Wolof Text Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Communications, Computing and Artificial Intelligence (CCCAI)
abstract: Sentiment analysis is an essential task in natural language processing. It aims to automatically evaluate the sentiment polarity. Several methods and tools have been developed to address this issue which is more difficult in a bilingual context, such as the case of Senegal where the official French language is often mixed with Wolof the national language. [1] has been recently proposed as effective solutions for overcoming the complexities of this bilingual sentiment analysis. The lemmatizer-methods used there are based respectively on word-level similarity and the word-level trigrams (list of consecutive three letters) to convert inflectional forms and derivationally related forms of a word to a common base form. This morphological analysis approach is very complex and has some limitations for normalizing some words because French words are morphologically complex. Furthermore, the lemmatization of Wolof words is very difficult to implement because they are written using the French alphabet. In addition, these previous approaches use Bayes independence assumption to determine the sentiment of a sentence. This is another limitation when considering syntactic rules in a linguistic expression. To overcome these drawbacks and address the challenges and opportunities of bilingual sentiment analysis, we propose: (i) a French-Wolof dictionary and dictionary-based lemmatizer for better deal with verbs’ conjugation or some words’ declination in both languages, and (ii) a method for determining context dependent sentiment words based on Markov Model. Experimental conducted on a more larger data [2], shows that it successfully predicts sentiment polarity with an accuracy of 0.94 (implying an increase of 21% compared to the previous work).

articleTitle: Deep Semi-Supervised Learning with Fine-Grained Dynamic Weights and Pseudo-Label Constraints
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Communications, Computing and Artificial Intelligence (CCCAI)
abstract: Semi-supervised learning is comonly trained using a large amount of unlabeled data and a small amount of labeled data. Existing works have achieved excellent results through consistent regularization methods. However, when designing the loss function, they set a loss function for labeled and unlabeled data separately, ignoring the connection between labeled and unlabeled data. Furthermore, unlabeled data all share the same weight, but the weights of different unlabeled data should be different. Based on these observations, a pair loss is proposed in this paper to strengthen the connection between labeled and unlabeled data; in addition, a dynamic weight is designed for each unlabeled data based on EMA (Exponential Moving Average) when calculating the loss function. Finally, a deep semi-supervised learning method called DWPC is proposed by combining dynamic weighting and pair loss. Experimental results on several datasets show that the proposed method improves performance in many scenarios.

articleTitle: GAM-YOLOv3: A Lightweight Object Detection Network based on GhostBottleneck and CBAM
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Communications, Computing and Artificial Intelligence (CCCAI)
abstract: In traditional convolutional neural networks, there is a contradiction that complex network detection is slow and basic network detection accuracy is low. We propose a lightweight object detection network GAM-YOLOv3. Firstly, GhostBottleneck replaces Residual block in Darknet-53 backbone network. It obviously diminishes parameters of the network model and effectively improves the detection speed. Secondly, by adopting the CBAM attention module to substitute the ordinary convolution layer in the original neck network. The network parameters continuously decrease. The accuracy decrease caused by simplified networks is effectively improved. Conclusively, Hard-Swish activation function enhances network model detection stability. Compared with YOLOv3, GAM-YOLOv3 network parameters are reduced by 50% overall. It greatly speeds up object detection and perfectly satisfies real-time detection tasks.

articleTitle: Contour Refinement for Box Based Interactive Object Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Communications, Computing and Artificial Intelligence (CCCAI)
abstract: As the development of interactive object segmentation, the optimization of the segmented contour draws much attention. Inspired by current interactive object segmentation and contour-based methods, this paper proposes an end-to-end framework for contour refinement for box based interactive object segmentation. Compared with traditional interactive object segmentation approaches, our method not only constrains the scope of segmentation in terms of region, but also controls and optimizes the deformational results of the contour, which achieves the goal of refined interactive object segmentation. We build a complete system including a contour extraction model and a contour deformation model. The initial contour extracted from the result of segmentation by the contour extraction model is fed to the contour deformation model for vertices offset and contour deformation. Meanwhile, we perform dynamic dilation for the initial contour before contour refinement to improve the feature information provided by the contour extraction model. In addition, we put the compactness of each contour as a reference factor into the point set sampled on the contour to solve the problem of over-sharp boundary. Experiments show that the proposed method achieves advanced performance for interactive object segmentation.

articleTitle: CvTSRR: A Convolutional Vision Transformer Based Method for Social Relation Recognition
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Communications, Computing and Artificial Intelligence (CCCAI)
abstract: Social relations refer to the relationships or interactions existing between people, such as family members, friends, coworkers, and so on. Social relationship analysis can provide understanding of human behaviors and therefore lead to many applications. With more and more people sharing images online, effectively recognizing social relations from the visual data becomes critical. Although a good number of studies had been carried out for social relationship recognition, the results are far from perfection. Better models need to be designed for feature extraction and image comprehension. In this paper, we propose a new learning model—CvTSRR for recognizing social relationships in images. This model employs a convolutional vision transformer (CvT) architecture to extract visual features and a multi-head attention mechanism to identify social relationships. The model was evaluated on a benchmark dataset called PISC (People in Social Context), and its performance was compared with those from previous works. Experimental results show that CvTSRR is competitive with the state-of-the-art models and outperforms them in several aspects.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of DNS Root Query Performance Between Continents
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Communications, Computing and Artificial Intelligence (CCCAI)
abstract: DNS root server provides network users with nearby resolution service through anycast root instances widely deployed around the world. This paper proposes a measurement method, which compares and analyzes the latency of root query on six different continents in the world from two aspects: latency distribution of DNS root queries and the latency penalty occurred when a query replied by an overseas root instance. In addition, we locate the relatively best and worst performing country or region in each continent.

articleTitle: Reinforcement Learning for Optimizing Age of Information and Energy Consumption in Misson-critical IoT
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Communications, Computing and Artificial Intelligence (CCCAI)
abstract: The emerging Internet of Things (IoT) play a vital role in remote monitoring. Age of Information (AoI) is an effective metric defined as the elapsed time since the generation of the packet by the transmitter. In this paper, we study a remote monitoring system consisting of a scheduling node and some sensor nodes. The scheduling algorithm strives to find the optimal trade-off between minimizing the sum of the expected AoI, the AoI violation probability, the transmission energy consumption of the sensor nodes and the cost of sensor node replacement due to battery drainage. We model the problem as a Markov Decision Process (MDP) with finite state and action spaces, and utilizes the certainty equivalence to approximate the stochastic reward. An actor-critic-based algorithm is proposed. Simulation results show that compared with the random scheduling policy and the policy which only considers minimizing sum of AoI and AoI violation probability, the proposed algorithm can optimize both AoI and energy more effectively.

articleTitle: Proposal for the design of an articulable robot for taking low-cost measurements in the preoperative phase of maxillofacial surgery
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Communications, Computing and Artificial Intelligence (CCCAI)
abstract: This research paper presents the design of an articulable robot for low-cost measurement in people needing maxillofacial surgery. It is observed that it is possible to improve the measurement accuracy, significantly reduce the error rate and risk to the patient, while reducing the manufacturing cost. This design presents a stable structure for the maxillofacial surgeon, an intuitive interface for the user, in addition to stepper motor actuators that allow the movement of the axes, worm screws and rack and pinion, where there is greater precision and speed, as well as a Raspberry Pi Pico W microprocessor that controls the articulating robot with great efficiency and with sufficient memory to store and carry out the purpose for which it was designed. In order to consolidate the objectives, set at the beginning, the mixed methodology between VDI 2206 and MIT was developed and used. The results obtained will not only serve to create articulable and controllable robots with low complexity costs, but also to reduce the error rate and reduce the risk for the patient, promoting the use of robotics in medicine and involving the new proposed methodology to research projects.

articleTitle: Feature Alignment and Contrastive Learning for Dense Instance Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Communications, Computing and Artificial Intelligence (CCCAI)
abstract: Instance segmentation is an important but challenging computer vision task. Existing approaches struggle to recognize independent objects in dense scenarios where objects are tightly in contact. In this paper, we propose a segmentation network called FAC-Mask. On the one hand, it incorporates a feature alignment module, which facilitates the network to effectively integrate multi-scale information. On the other hand, we design a contrastive learning module to assist the segmentation head in feature representation learning, by learning common features among similar instances and distinguishing differences between non-similar instances. We conduct experiments on the Cityspace dataset, our model improves the detection and segmentation accuracy by +2.4% and +2.8% when fused with RefineMask. The results have demonstrated the efficacy of our method.

articleTitle: Energy Saving Research on Auxiliary Task Unloading and Resource Allocation of UAV Based on Edge Computing
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Communications, Computing and Artificial Intelligence (CCCAI)
abstract: In order to improve the effectiveness of task unloading and the reliability of resource allocation in the UAV auxiliary system based on edge computing, this paper studies the problem of multi task and multi service task unloading with multiple edge servers in a multi UAV auxiliary environment, and sums up the problem as minimizing the system delay under the constraint of system energy consumption while maximizing the system efficiency. To solve this problem, firstly, the delay is minimized while considering communication, queuing, switching, computation, and transmission delays, and resource allocation and offloading strategies are optimized through particle swarm optimization considering service placement points and access points; Secondly, the flight path of UAV is planned by Ant colony optimization algorithms to reduce the system energy consumption. In addition, in order to better balance the two indicators of time delay and energy consumption, weights will be added when calculating the system efficiency. From the simulation results, it can be seen that the proposed method can effectively improve the effectiveness of task offloading and the reliability of resource allocation.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Prediction of LOS Probability in Urban Environments
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Communications, Computing and Artificial Intelligence (CCCAI)
abstract: Prediction of line-of-sight (LOS) probability is an important topic in wireless communication. With more scatterers and obstacles in urban environment and with increasingly complex building distribution, it brings in more difficulties into LOS prediction at different base stations. Consequently, 3GPP d<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>/d<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> statistical model might lead to larger error. Therefore, in this paper, we propose a machine-learning-based approach for LOS probability approximation in outdoor environment based on measurements obtained from geographic information data from California, Washington and Florida city areas. Support vector machine (SVM) and gradient boosted decision trees (GBDT) models are used to compare against an artificial-neural-network-based (ANN-based) model. The ANN-based model is finally employed to predict the LOS probability in urban environment based on the features of building footprints, terrain, and antenna towers, etc. Compared to the 3GPP d<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>/d<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> model in error cumulative distribution function (CDF) curves, the proposed model provides a more accurate LOS approximation to the real world LOS distributions.

articleTitle: Multi-view Canonical Representation Discriminant Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Communications, Computing and Artificial Intelligence (CCCAI)
abstract: Multi-view classification that classifies samples from heterogeneous views is still a challenging problem in computer vision. The multi-view discriminant analysis is an effective method for this problem based on seeking a common subspace for multi-view data. However, existing methods usually fail to learn optimal discriminant projection matrix due to the possible singularity of the within-class scatter matrix. In this paper, we propose a novel multi-view canonical representation discriminant analysis (MCRDA) approach.Specially, our MCRDA joins the supervised information with common representation extraction to obtain a discriminant common subspace. By utilizing the equivalence of least squares regression (LSR) and linear discriminant analysis (LDA), an efficient iterative optimization algorithm is proposed to solve the method, we perform extensive experiments on several benchmark data sets in comparison with some state-of the-art multi-view discriminant analysis methods. Experimental results illustrate that the proposed method shows promising classification performance.

articleTitle: CLGP: Multi-Feature Embedding based Cross-Attention for Chinese NER
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Communications, Computing and Artificial Intelligence (CCCAI)
abstract: The previous works fused lexicon information while ignoring two important Chinese language characteristics: glyph and pinyin, which carry significant syntax and semantics information for sequence tagging tasks. This paper proposes CLGP, which utilizes four specific extractors to obtain the embeddings of character, glyph, pinyin, and lexicon, and further uses a network based on cross-attention to perform the multi-embedding fusion. Specifically, we introduce the embedding scheme to preserve the lexicon-matching results and design two specific CNN to extract glyph and pinyin embeddings. Moreover, we fuse the four embeddings by the cross-attention-based network to enhance the Chinese NER. The experimental results on four famous datasets show that CLGP achieves state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance.

articleTitle: Efficient Dialogue State Tracking based on Dialogue-level State Prediction and Historical Dialogue State Deletion
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Communications, Computing and Artificial Intelligence (CCCAI)
abstract: The dialogue state tracking module is a crucial component of task-oriented dialogue systems. Recently, some Dialogue State Tracking (DST) methods have used the previous dialogue state as auxiliary input, resulting in errors that propagate and subsequently affect predictions. This paper proposes utilizing dialogue-level state as the prediction target and randomly removing historical dialogue state during training. The experiments demonstrate that this approach can effectively enhance the performance of the DST algorithm, alleviate error propagation, and achieve competitive results on both noisy (MultiWOZ 2.1) and clean (MultiWOZ 2.4) datasets.

articleTitle: HFLIC: Human Friendly Perceptual Learned Image Compression with Reinforced Transform
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Communications, Computing and Artificial Intelligence (CCCAI)
abstract: In recent years, there has been rapid development in learned image compression techniques that prioritize rate-distortion-perceptual compression, preserving fine details even at lower bit-rates. However, current learning-based image compression methods often sacrifice human-friendly compression and require long decoding times. In this paper, we propose enhancements to the backbone network and loss function of existing image compression model, focusing on improving human perception and efficiency. Our proposed approach achieves competitive subjective results compared to state-of-the-art end-to-end learned image compression methods and classic methods, while requiring less decoding time and offering human-friendly compression. Through empirical evaluation, we demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed method in achieving outstanding performance, with more than 25% bit-rate saving with comparable perceptual quality.

articleTitle: Infrared Small Target Detection Based on Facet Kernel and Global Contrast Measure
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Communications, Computing and Artificial Intelligence (CCCAI)
abstract: The current state of infrared small target detection methods suffers from limitations in background suppression and multi-target detection capabilities, resulting in a high false alarm rate and high omission factor within infrared search and track systems. To address these issues, a new method known as facet global contrast measure (FGCM) was proposed. Through extensive experimentation, it was found that this method resulted in a significant improvement in performance, with an average increase of 2.95 times in background suppression factor and 6.17 times in signal-to-clutter ratio gain for single-target detection, and 10.49 times for multi-target detection, when compared to similar detection methods.

articleTitle: Utilizing deep learning for automated tuning of database management systems
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Communications, Computing and Artificial Intelligence (CCCAI)
abstract: Managing the configurations of a database system poses significant challenges due to the multitude of configuration knobs that impact various system aspects. The lack of standardization, independence, and universality among these knobs further complicates the task of determining the optimal settings. To address this issue, an automated solution leveraging supervised and unsupervised machine learning techniques was developed. This solution aims to identify influential knobs, analyze previously unseen workloads, and provide recommendations for knob settings. The effectiveness of this approach is demonstrated through the evaluation of a new tool called OtterTune [1] on three different database management systems (DBMSs). The results indicate that OtterTune’s recommendations are comparable to or even surpass the configurations generated by existing tools or human experts. In this study, we build upon the automated technique introduced in the original OtterTune paper, utilizing previously collected training data to optimize new DBMS deployments. By employing supervised and unsupervised machine learning methods, we focus on improving latency prediction. Our approach expands upon the methods proposed in the original paper by incorporating GMM clustering to streamline metrics selection and combining ensemble models (such as RandomForest) with non-linear models (like neural networks) for more accurate prediction modeling.

articleTitle: EAD-YOLO: Improved YOLOv5 for Endoscopic Artefact Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Communications, Computing and Artificial Intelligence (CCCAI)
abstract: Endoscopic artefacts seriously affect the visualization of the lesion area during endoscopy and the results of automated detection and analysis. Therefore, accurate detection of clinical endoscopic artefacts has become a key bottleneck. In this paper, aiming at the problems of data imbalance and severe multi-scale distribution of objects in the endoscope artefact dataset, we propose a multi-scale detection algorithm EADYOLO. Based on the baseline network YOLOv5, the algorithm has been improved in three aspects. First, the data imbalance is alleviated by adopting data augmentation methods. Second, by constructing a multi-scale detection layer to improve the detection effect of the algorithm on endoscopic artefact targets of different scales. The depthwise separable convolution is used to reduce the number of parameters of the network and improve the feature extraction capability of the backbone network. Finally, Atrous Spatial Pyramid Pooling (ASPP) module is used to further enhance the expression ability of multi-scale target features. Compared with the baseline network, EAD-YOLO can improve the detection accuracy and recall rate of small and large targets by 3.23%, 7.64%, 2.37%, and 4.45% respectively. The comparison with classical and effective algorithms further proves that EAD-YOLO can better adapt to the severe size changes of endoscopic artefacts, and is more beneficial to the task of endoscopic artefact target detection.

articleTitle: Automated Lineage Inference among Malware Families
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Communications, Computing and Artificial Intelligence (CCCAI)
abstract: To effectively expand illegal proceeds, current malware has exhibited a trend of modular derivation, resulting in a continuous reduction in the time cycle from design to completion of a new family. The rapid evolution of malware families makes lineage analysis urgent for security practitioners. However, the techniques are still in the exploratory stage; their applicability is limited due to the lack of automated methods. As time passes and malware evolves, the insights gained from such methods will become less applicable to new situations, and their reference value will be greatly reduced. In this paper, we propose an automated approach to analyzing the lineage relationship among malware families and apply our approach to a Windows malware dataset of more than 57,000 samples. The experimental results prove that our approach can effectively extract the core functions of samples and reasonably infer the association relationship among different families.

articleTitle: Chinese Event Extraction Method based on Abstract Meaning Representation Graph
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Communications, Computing and Artificial Intelligence (CCCAI)
abstract: Most of Chinese event extraction methods mainly focus on syntactic information and pay scant attention to semantic information. To make full use of semantic information, we take event extraction as a sequence labeling task and propose a Chinese event extraction method based on abstract meaning representation to improve the accuracy and recall rate of event extraction tasks. The model generates abstract meaning representation graph for input sentences, and the graph attention mechanism is used to capture semantic relationships, extract event argument elements and event triggers, and improve the prediction ability of the model. Compared with the baseline models, the accuracy rate, recall rate and F1-score of ACE2005 Chinese set is significant increased, especially in argument classification, with 11.4%, 13.4%, and 12.5% respectively, which verified the effectiveness of our method.

articleTitle: A Novel Face Recognition Model Based on Feature Registration
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Communications, Computing and Artificial Intelligence (CCCAI)
abstract: With the rapid development of information construction, identity identification has become an important factor affecting the economic and social security in the era of big data. Face recognition is the core research direction in the field of identity authentication and image processing security. In recent years, the research of face recognition mainly focuses on how to eliminate the influence of environmental factors and facial occlusion. A face detection model based on feature registration is proposed, which uses Gaussian filter processing to realize image noise reduction, and introduces the improved Prewitt operator edge detection to realize binarization. Through the gray level threshold separation and screening of specific areas, on the basis of position determination, location of face organs and parameters were analyzed, and the face recognition model was constructed, and puts forward the improved Harris corner feature extraction methods in combination with Normalized Cross Correlation face matching normalization algorithm. The experimental effect showed that the experimental accuracy reached 90.13%, and time efficiency was increased by 6.67%.

articleTitle: Classifying user interaction activity in task mining
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Communications, Computing and Artificial Intelligence (CCCAI)
abstract: In this work, we have developed a solution to facilitate Digital Process Management and Task Mining by categorizing User Interaction Activities in User Interface. To achieve this goal, we have created an internal dataset of User Interaction Activities. The user interactions are determined by screenshots that have been taken by an internal Task Mining recording software. To categorize the User Interaction Activities of various applications and interaction types, we used the modern Computer Vision approach. To develop the dataset we took leverage of classical image process methods. We have compared successful and promising Computer Vision methods in our dataset considering its traits. Classifying such user interactions in a human-understandable way opens a vast range of possibilities in the field of digital Task Mining and Analysis.

articleTitle: Solving the Multi-tasking Robust Optimization on Networks via Structural Reconstructions using a Multi-factor Evolutionary Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Communications, Computing and Artificial Intelligence (CCCAI)
abstract: Networks tend to be operated in complicated environments, where attacks and errors threaten their functionality. Previous studies indicated that structural damages may impair the performance of networks, and the information propagation process is at risk. The corresponding optimization tasks are modeled as the network robustness optimization problem and the robust influence maximization problem, respectively. These two problems are of great significance in theory and practice and have attracted increasing attention in recent studies. However, existing approaches are far from comprehensive. The impact of structural perturbances on the information propagation process has not been thoroughly investigated. The determination of robust seeds against topological failures remains an open question. Meanwhile, the possible parallelism between the two robust optimization problems has been completely ignored in the current research. Therefore, the multi-tasking optimization theory is employed in this work to tackle the above challenges. The correlative relationship between the two problems is analyzed, and a positive correlation is detected. Further, a multi-factor evolutionary algorithm with multiple problem-oriented operators, named MFEA-Net, is developed to solve both network robustness optimization problems and robust influence maximization problems simultaneously. Experimental results demonstrate that the algorithm is competitive compared with other methods, which contributes to the solution of diffusion problems on networks.

articleTitle: A benchmark study of protein folding algorithms on nanobodies
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Communications, Computing and Artificial Intelligence (CCCAI)
abstract: Nanobodies, also known as single-domain or VHH antibodies, are recombinant variable domains derived from heavy-chain-only antibodies. They exhibit desirable characteristics, including small size, high solubility, exceptional stability, rapid blood clearance, and deep tissue penetration, rendering them valuable tools for disease diagnosis and treatment. In recent years, several deep-learning-based methods for protein structure prediction have been developed, requiring only protein sequences as input. Notable examples include AlphaFold2, RoseTTAFold, DeepAb, NanoNet, and tFold, which have demonstrated remarkable performance in protein or antibody/nanobody prediction. In this study, we analyzed 60 nanobody samples with known experimental 3D structures from the Protein Data Bank (PDB). The accuracy of these algorithms was assessed using two metrics: RMSD and TM-score. Our findings revealed that NanoNet and tFold, particularly NanoNet, exhibit outstanding performance.

articleTitle: Design and Control of Multi-mode Wheeled-Bipedal Robot with Parallel Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Communications, Computing and Artificial Intelligence (CCCAI)
abstract: Wheeled-bipedal robot is a kind of mobile robot to combine the advantages of wheeled and legged locomotion. However, existing wheeled bipedal robots often require effort to overcome gravity while they do not need to maintain a standing position all the time. Therefore, we design a multimode motor-driven wheeled-bipedal robot SUSTech-Nezha II to explore the fusion of wheel and leg. The robot has two mirror symmetric legs with a total of six degrees of freedom. A novel five-bar linkage mechanism has been integrated into the design of the leg for the purpose of transmission. The robot has two modes of motion: the wheeled-bipedal mode and the four-wheel mode. The robot primarily operates in the four-wheel mode, as it provides superior stability and energy efficiency compared to the wheeled-bipedal mode. The latter mode is only utilized when height adjustments are necessary. This paper introduces the design and control methods of the overall robotic system. The control strategy for seamless mode switching is also developed. Finally, we verify the feasibility of the whole system through several hardware experiments.
